stem.text: Water is pumped into a tank at a rate of R(t) liters per minute, where R is a positive function and t is measured in minutes. Using correct units, interpret the meaning of \( \int_{0}^{3} R(t)\,dt \) in the context of the problem.

answer_key.label: It is the total amount of water pumped into the tank from \( t = 0 \) to \( t = 3 \) minutes, measured in liters.

worked_solution.text: R(t) is a rate measured in liters per minute, so integrating it over time multiplies by minutes and gives an amount in liters.
worked_solution.rule_named: units of a definite integral of a rate

worked_solution.text: The limits run from \( t = 0 \) to \( t = 3 \) minutes, so \( \int_{0}^{3} R(t)\,dt \) is the total amount of water pumped into the tank from \( t = 0 \) to \( t = 3 \) minutes.
worked_solution.rule_named: integral of a rate is the accumulated change

worked_solution.text: The units are liters per minute times minutes, which is liters.
